transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Laura (Finovia Head of Security), Omar (Finovia Platform), Sofia (Finovia Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick security review focused on where data is stored/processed, whether Redwood can guarantee EU residency and pinning, questions around BYOK and sub-processors, and operational controls for audit logs.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro \u0004 I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Daniel, our solutions engineer.
00:18 - Laura Schmidt: Hi, thanks. we're mainly concerned about data residency, we operate across EU and US and need guarantees that PII and transactional content doesn't leave the EU region unless we explicitly allow it.
00:30 - Daniel Brooks: yep, understood. quick caveat \u0004 i'll try to use plain language, but we also have a security pack i'll share. So, Redwood supports region pinning at the org and route level, so you can have requests land and be processed only in eu-west-1, for example.
00:52 - Omar Ruiz: is that per-request or per-deployment? like can we pin specific endpoints for EU customers and others for US?
01:05 - Daniel Brooks: both \u0004 you can pin by deployment / model route. routing policy will keep the KV cache and inference execution in the pinned region. there's a small note: fallbacks can be configured; by default we won't cross-pin unless you opt in for cross-region fallback.
01:30 - Laura Schmidt: what about cross-border processing for things like telemetry or metadata? logs? we need to ensure those don't get shipped to US sub-processors.
01:45 - Maya Chen: good question. we do have sub-processors \u0004 primary cloud providers (AWS, GCP) and some managed logging partners. we can restrict where audit logs are stored and we support exporting logs to your SIEM in-region. we'll include our sub-processor list in the DPA.
02:10 - Sofia Petrov: legal question \u0004 do you rely on SCCs or other transfer mechanisms for EU->US flows?
02:22 - Daniel Brooks: currently we use standard contractual clauses and our DPA references SCCs + updated transfer mechanisms; when customers require, we can accommodate additional contractual language, and for high-risk flows we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to eliminate cross-border routing.
02:45 - Omar Ruiz: Dedicated as in reserved capacity in a single region? how much effort to stand that up for a POC?
02:57 - Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools pinned to region and customer. for POC we can reserve a small pool in eu-west-1. usually timeline is 1-2 weeks for basic provisioning, depends on networking (VPC peering or private link).
03:20 - Laura Schmidt: encryption \u0004 we need keys that we control. do you support BYOK / customer-managed KMS?
03:30 - Daniel Brooks: yes, we support BYOK. you can bring your own keys via your KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and tie it to storage and model artifact encryption. for hosted we have an option to integrate with your KMS via cross-account roles; for Private deployments you manage keys entirely.
03:52 - Sofia Petrov: any caching that could leak data across tenants? how is the KV cache handled?
04:05 - Daniel Brooks: KV cache is tenancy isolated. for shared-hosted we have strict multi-tenant isolation and per-tenant cache namespaces; for stricter needs you can opt for dedicated pools where the runtime instances and caches are dedicated to your org.
04:30 - Laura Schmidt: audit logs \u0004 retention and where they live. we require 7 years for certain logs and ability to export to our SIEM and to redact sensitive fields.
04:45 - Maya Chen: we currently have configurable retention policies and can export logs via secure transfer to your S3 bucket or SIEM. redaction \u0004 we provide filters and PII masking hooks; we should cover specifics in the security whitepaper.
05:08 - Omar Ruiz: who are your sub-processors specifically for eu hosting? are you colocating with AWS only or GCP as well?
05:20 - Daniel Brooks: we use AWS heavily in eu-west-1 for hosted; we also can run on GCP in customer requests. the sub-processor list will be in the DPA, but common ones are AWS, GCP, Datadog for metrics (optional), and a managed logging vendor for archived logs.
05:45 - Laura Schmidt: any data sent to model evaluation/benchmarks goes out of region? we run evals on prompt sets and those sometimes contain IP.
06:00 - Daniel Brooks: evaluation prompts can be kept in-region; we don't route them to US unless configured. we also have an eval mode that runs in a sealed environment \u0004 we can discuss that for sensitive workloads.
06:20 - Sofia Petrov: regarding subprocessors \u0004 do you notify customers ahead of onboarding new ones?
06:28 - Maya Chen: yes, our DPA includes notification windows for new sub-processors and you can request review. we also publish a sub-processor change log.
06:40 - Omar Ruiz: what about telemetry \u0004 heartbeat metrics and usage stats \u0004 are those considered business data? do they leave region?
06:50 - Daniel Brooks: by default some aggregated telemetry is used for platform health and may cross regions, but for enterprise customers we can toggle to keep telemetry in-region and ship metrics to your telemetry backend instead.
07:10 - Laura Schmidt: SSO/SSAML \u0004 we use Okta and need SCIM + SAML for provisioning and SSO. does Redwood support that?
07:20 - Maya Chen: yes, SAML + SCIM supported, RBAC via groups and roles. we also support SCIM provisioning and audit trails for admin activity.
07:40 - Omar Ruiz: any notes about encryption in transit \u0004 TLS only or mutual TLS?
07:48 - Daniel Brooks: TLS 1.2/1.3 for default. mTLS can be enabled for dedicated/private deployments, and private link options are available for network isolation.
08:05 - Laura Schmidt: okay, can we get an architecture diagram that shows data flow, specifically where the model artifacts live, where logs land, and key management?
08:15 - Maya Chen: yes, we'll include an architecture diagram in the follow-up pack.
08:25 - Sofia Petrov: DPA questions \u0004 do you accept a customer's DPA or is it your standard?
08:33 - Maya Chen: we start from our standard DPA but we do negotiate material clauses for enterprise customers; for Finovia we can have legal review.
08:44 - Omar Ruiz: about region pinning \u0004 how is it enforced on the runtime side? like is routing rule evaluated at the gateway?
08:54 - Daniel Brooks: routing occurs at the edge and control plane. requests include org and route metadata; the control plane maps to a serving cluster and enforces region constraints. we use signed routing policies and audit every mapping change.
09:15 - Laura Schmidt: is that mapping visible to customers? can we audit changes?
09:22 - Daniel Brooks: yes, audit logs include routing and deployment changes; we can stream audit events to your log sink.
09:35 - Maya Chen: quick interruption \u0004 just to note, some customers want absolute guarantees of no cross-border processing; for them we recommend Private (on-prem) or Dedicated single-region with BYOK to reduce legal surface.
09:50 - Laura Schmidt: makes sense. what about backups and snapshots \u0004 do they replicate across regions?
09:58 - Daniel Brooks: backups don't replicate cross-region unless you enable cross-region disaster recovery; by default for region-pinned deployments snapshots are retained in-region. we'll include backup policy details in the doc pack.
10:20 - Omar Ruiz: are there any sub processors in the US that could see metadata in logs even if data is in EU?
10:30 - Daniel Brooks: if you use our managed logging archival (hosted), archived logs may be stored with the logging partner \u0004 we can configure archives to stay in EU or export to your bucket. for strict requirements, we recommend direct export to your in-region bucket or use our dedicated logging pipelines.
10:50 - Laura Schmidt: can you do per-route encryption keys? we have different data classifications and want separate keys per project.
11:02 - Daniel Brooks: yes, per-route or per-tenant key scoping is supported in BYOK configurations. we'll discuss the exact implementation with your infra team.
11:20 - Sofia Petrov: from a legal standpoint we'll need the sub-processor list and a commitment on notification timelines; i'll draft the questions and share.
11:30 - Maya Chen: perfect. we'll include the list and notification cadence.
11:40 - Omar Ruiz: planning \u0004 assuming we run a POC in eu-west-1 with region pinning and BYOK, what's the minimal data we need to share to get started?
11:52 - Daniel Brooks: we need a network contact for VPC peering/private link, sample traffic (QPS, payload sizes), SSO/SCIM admin contact, and the KMS account details if you want BYOK.
12:12 - Laura Schmidt: SLA and data retention \u0004 do you have SOC2 type II? encryption standards?
12:20 - Maya Chen: yes SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 \u0004 we'll attach certs. encryption at rest via AES-256, TLS in transit; BYOK as discussed.
12:35 - Omar Ruiz: one more \u0004 are model updates or model variant fallbacks ever processed outside the pinned region? e.g., if we use a cached KV and a model variant exists only in us, would it route?
12:50 - Daniel Brooks: model variants can be configured; by default we won't route to variants outside the pinned region unless you enable cross-region fallback. you can also pin to model family versions.
13:10 - Maya Chen: ok we're approaching the end \u0004 high level next steps, we'll send SOC2/ISO and DPA, sub-processor list, architecture diagram, and schedule a KMS deep dive.
13:28 - Laura Schmidt: thanks. Sofia and I will review docs and follow up with legal questions.
13:35 - Sofia Petrov: thanks \u0004 can you also include a sample DPA with SCC references?
13:40 - Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll include that.
13:45 - Omar Ruiz: i'll email the sample traffic numbers and infra contacts.
13:50 - Maya Chen: great thanks everyone. we'll aim to get the pack out by Friday.
14:00 - (meeting ends)
